title: How Ensemble Learning Balances Accuracy and Overfitting: A Bias-Variance Perspective on Tabular Data
summary: Tree-based ensembles are often strong on tabular data, but the paper asks when their variance reduction actually improves test accuracy and reduces overfitting. It compares single models with nine ensembles on four public tabular datasets using five-seed repeated stratified cross-validation, dataset-complexity metrics, and Wilcoxon tests. The main result is three regimes: near-linear Breast Cancer gives no significant ensemble gain (RBF SVM 0.972 test accuracy), structured nonlinear Heart Disease gains 5–7 points, and noisy/imbalanced data require regularization and minority-class metrics.

match_target.why: Cheapest target: one RBF-SVM model on the smallest dataset, and it is the paper's rank-1 Breast Cancer result for the clean/near-linear regime.

tolerance.why: Rule 1: the paper reports ±0.008 std over five seeds for the target; 3 × 0.008 = 0.024, rounded to the printed 3-decimal precision.

requirements.stmt: Use the four main datasets with the sizes and feature counts reported in Table I.
requirements.quote: This dataset contains 569 instances with 30 real-valued features

requirements.stmt: Apply z-score standardization inside scikit-learn pipelines for LR, KNN, and SVM; keep tree-based models on original scales.
requirements.quote: Distance-based and linear models (LR, KNN, SVM) use z-score standardization via scikit-learn pipelines.

requirements.stmt: Use stratified k-fold cross-validation repeated over five seeds 42, 123, 456, 789, and 1011 for the three smaller datasets.
requirements.quote: We use stratified k-fold cross-validation with five independent random seeds (42, 123, 456, 789, 1011) to estimate generalization and quantify uncertainty.

requirements.stmt: For Credit Card Fraud, use a 10% stratified subsample, 3-fold stratified CV, and a single seed.
requirements.cite: Sec. V-B and Table III footnote
requirements.quote: a 10% stratified subsample that preserves class imbalance, followed by three-fold stratified CV with a single seed

requirements.stmt: Compare the single-model baselines against the nine ensemble methods described in the paper.
requirements.quote: We compare the following models, chosen to represent commonly used baselines and ensembles

requirements.stmt: Implement SVM with an RBF kernel, probability calibration, and standardized features.
requirements.quote: SVM (RBF): RBF-kernel SVM with probability calibration; features standardized.

requirements.stmt: Handle class imbalance with class weights and scale_pos_weight as specified.
requirements.quote: scale_pos_weight in XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost set to the negative-to-positive ratio.

requirements.stmt: Run light GridSearchCV over compact grids rather than exhaustive optimization.
requirements.quote: We perform light hyperparameter tuning with GridSearchCV over compact grids

requirements.stmt: Use Random Forests with 200–400 trees and tune depth.
requirements.quote: For Random Forests, we use nestimators = 200–400 with depth tuning

requirements.stmt: Define the overfitting gap as train accuracy minus test accuracy.
Use paired two-tailed Wilcoxon signed-rank tests at α = 0.05 for top-model comparisons.
requirements.quote: pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (α = 0.05, two-tailed) between the top-performing models on each dataset

requirements.stmt: Compute the five dataset-complexity indicators used to explain the regimes.
requirements.quote: To understand why different datasets fall into different generalization regimes, we compute five dataset-complexity indicators

requirements.stmt: Implement Stacking with LR, Decision Tree, and RBF SVM base learners, LR meta-learner, and passthrough features.
requirements.quote: LR, Decision Tree, and RBF SVM as base learners, with LR meta-learner and passthrough of original features.

requirements.stmt: Make the implementation and result summaries available reproducibly.
requirements.quote: Full code, result summaries, complexity metrics, and statistical test results are publicly available

requirements.stmt: For Credit Card Fraud, emphasize fraud-class F1, recall, ROC-AUC, and PR-AUC rather than accuracy alone.
requirements.quote: We focus on fraud-class F1, recall, ROC-AUC, and PR-AUC rather than accuracy alone.
